evidence.note: Environment probing was minimal: ls /app, checked for start.sh, pip-installed deps, then immediately began writing models.py and server.py. No systematic extraction of the contract's hard constraints (status-code matrix, envelope keys, seq invariant, role matrix, IRC numerics) before committing to a design.

Repeated slash-command bugs (regular messages treated as 'unknown' commands, action[0] on None) show the /me, /shrug, //literal semantics were not read/internalized before coding — a subtle rule misread, discovered only at runtime after building.

The full testid inventory was handled reactively: agent counted testids only after building, found critical ones (emoji-picker, reaction-chip, invitation-code, settings panes) missing, then patched them via sed/python. This proves the pinned frontend-hook list was not internalized upfront.

Did probe the runtime post-build (health across all three node_ids, cross-node propagation, an IRC login test), showing some environment verification, but no deliberate modeling of the dense-per-channel-seq-across-nodes-and-IRC invariant, the 5s broadcaster-kill bound, or node-kill resilience — these were built as a 'broadcast helper' without any reasoning surfaced about the invariants they must satisfy.

reasoning: The agent skimmed the contract enough to get obvious routes and roughly correct envelopes (register→{user,token}, health→node_id), placing it above 0, but it clearly misread or ignored subtle rules: slash-command literal semantics caused runtime bugs, the testid inventory was discovered and patched reactively rather than captured upfront, and the dense-seq/resilience invariants were never explicitly modeled or cross-referenced before building. This matches the level-3 anchor (skims contract, gets obvious routes, misreads/ignores subtle rules like dense seq, /shrug text, and the testid list) rather than level 5, which requires deliberately capturing the seq invariant, resilience expectations, and pinned hooks before building.
